request_outcomes.question: Do you take Cigna insurance?
request_outcomes.answer:
Yes, we take Cigna for medical care, with some conditions: we're in-network with Cigna Open Access Plus (OAP) and Cigna PPO plans. Cigna LocalPlus plans are in-network only if you live in our county (check the network area on the back of your card). Cigna Connect plans purchased through the health insurance marketplace are not in-network.

For dental care, we do not accept Cigna Dental Care DHMO.

citations.chunk_text:
Question: Which health insurance plans do you accept?
Answer: We accept most major insurance providers, including Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, and Medicare. If you're unsure whether your specific plan is covered, you can ask me to connect you with a member of our friendly front desk team. They'll be happy to help clarify your coverage.

# Insurance plan guide
## Cigna

We are in-network with Cigna Open Access Plus (OAP) and Cigna PPO plans. Cigna LocalPlus plans are in-network only for members who live in our county; the network area is printed on the back of the card. Cigna Connect plans bought through the health insurance marketplace are not in-network.

# Dental care guide
## Dental insurance

Medical insurance plans do not cover dental care. For dental appointments we accept these dental plans: Delta Dental PPO, MetLife PDP Plus and Guardian DentalGuard Preferred. We do not accept dental HMO (DHMO) plans, including Cigna Dental Care DHMO. If you do not hold one of the accepted dental plans, dental appointments are self-pay.

request_outcomes.question: When do I pay?
request_outcomes.answer: Payment is due at the time of service.

citations.chunk_text:
Question: When is payment due, and what payment methods do you accept?
Answer: Payment is due at the time of service. We accept cash, major credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express), and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) / Health Savings Account (HSA) cards.

# Insurance plan guide
## Copays and deductibles

Your plan decides how much you pay at the visit. A copay is a fixed amount your plan sets for each visit, and it is collected when you check in. If your plan has a deductible you have not met yet, you pay the amount your plan allows for the visit at check-in. The front desk can estimate that amount for you if you give them your plan details before the visit.

# General practice services
## Medical examinations for work, driving and sport

We do not carry out commercial driver (DOT) medical examinations, pilot medicals or immigration medical examinations. A sports physical before joining a team or a competition is done in a standard GP appointment.

Question: What should I do if my insurance isn't listed or I am out-of-network?
Answer: You can pay out-of-pocket for your visit, and we can provide you with an itemized receipt to submit to your insurer for potential reimbursement.

Question: How much will my visit cost if I am paying out-of-pocket?
Answer: Out-of-pocket rates are $120 for a General Practitioner (GP) visit, $180 for a Dentist appointment, and $160 for all other specialist consultations.

# General practice services
## Long-term conditions

If you live with a long-term condition such as type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, asthma or COPD, your GP will agree a regular review schedule with you, usually every three or six months. Bring your home blood pressure or blood glucose readings to each review, and bring your inhalers if you have asthma or COPD, so the GP can check your technique.

Cigna LocalPlus plans are in-network only if you live in our county (check the network area on the back of your card), and Cigna Connect plans purchased through the health insurance marketplace are not in-network. For dental care, we do not accept Cigna Dental Care DHMO.

As for payment, it's due at the time of service.
